sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi via Kilo, hold short of runway 27.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, cleared for takeoff runway 27, no delay, traffic six miles on final.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Granite Control, descend to flight level 240, cross MARLO at or below flight level 260.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Lakeside Airport via the ORCHID TWO departure, maintain 6,000, departure frequency 124.35, squawk 4512.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: You are being vectored for the approach into Bridgeport. The tower has just changed the landing runway. Now ATC contacts you. Acknowledge and respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Harbor Approach, runway change, expect ILS runway 09, new altimeter 29.92, there is a disabled aircraft on runway 27.

While taxiing out at Bridgeport you saw a large piece of rubber debris lying on taxiway Mike, close to the holding point. You were already cleared to line up, so you could not report it at the time. You are now airborne on the departure frequency. Acknowledge the clearance and report what you saw on the ground.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, Bridgeport Departure, radar contact, climb and maintain flight level 190.

You are level at flight level 290. There is a line of towering cumulus directly ahead of you with tops well above flight level 350, so you cannot climb over it. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly with a reason.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Granite Control, climb and maintain flight level 350 for traffic.

Approach instructed you to maintain 170 knots until five miles from touchdown. You are now on final with a strong tailwind and you had to reduce to 150 knots to stay on the approach profile. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 170 knots?
150 knots / tailwind

Granite Control cleared you to descend to flight level 200. You set 18,000 in the altitude window by mistake and the aircraft is now descending through flight level 195. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Granite Control, say your altitude.

Your en route clearance includes a waypoint called VANDO. Your flight management computer holds two waypoints with very similar names and you are not sure which one is on your route. You are level at flight level 310 and the waypoint is twelve minutes ahead. Contact Granite Control. Verify the waypoint and make a request so that you can be sure of it.
VANDO

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 3 flight stages: Cruise, Descent, Approach.
Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 330 and approaching TOPAZ, the first fix of the arrival into Lakeside Airport. You have not yet received the arrival information.

body.text: Contact Granite Control, report your position and request descent.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Granite Control, descend to flight level 190, cross TOPAZ at or below flight level 240, Lakeside information Romeo is current.
Listen to the controller's message, respond accordingly and request the information you still need.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, descend and maintain 11,000, contact Harbor Approach on 125.4.
unable to receive ATIS / request landing information

pre.text: Situation Update The controller has passed you information Romeo. The landing runway is 09 and the wind is 070 at 8. You are now descending through flight level 150 for 11,000.

body.text: Contact Harbor Approach and report your passing altitude.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Harbor Approach, good morning, descend and maintain 5,000, reduce speed to 220 knots, expect the TOPAZ ONE arrival, ILS runway 09, Lakeside altimeter 30.06.

pre.text: Situation Update The wind has backed round and is now 160 at 18, gusting 26. That is more crosswind than the tower is willing to use on runway 09.

body.text: Listen to the controller's message, respond accordingly and advise what you need.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Harbor Approach, we are changing the landing runway to 14 because of the wind, it will be an RNAV approach, and I have to take you around for the sequence, sorry about that.
Listen to the controller's question and respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept a short approach if the Embraer ahead of you gets off the runway in time? It would save you about eight miles.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, cleared for the RNAV runway 14 approach, maintain 170 knots to 5 miles, contact Lakeside Tower on 118.75.

pre.text: Situation Update You are established on the final approach course for runway 14 and passing 2,400 feet.

body.text: Contact Lakeside Tower, report your position and intention.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback. Then inquire about the aircraft you can see ahead on the runway.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Lakeside Tower, hello, wind 160 at 16, runway 14, cleared to land. The Embraer ahead is a little slow vacating, keep your speed up if you can.

Follow-up question: You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three. In this situation, the controller changed your landing runway late in the arrival. What did you have to do to get ready for the new approach, and why did you ask for the information you asked for? From your own experience, how late is too late for a runway change? Give an example.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, descending through flight level 160 to 9,000, inbound to Clearwater Airport. You have information Delta.

body.text: Contact Clearwater Approach and report your position.
Listen to the controller's response and respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Clearwater Approach, good afternoon, descend and maintain 7,000, expect the ILS runway 09, Clearwater altimeter 29.94.
ILS runway 09

pre.text: Situation Update As you level off at 7,000 you get a HYDRAULIC SYSTEM B LOW PRESSURE caution. The system B quantity is still falling and the standby pump has not brought the pressure back.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, state that you are levelling off at 7,000, and request time to work the checklist.
Listen to the controller's response, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, maintain 7,000, fly heading 270, that will keep you clear of the arrival stream, and say your intentions when you are ready.
Listen to the controller and respond negatively with a reason. Request what you need instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, runway 09 just went out of service, disabled aircraft on it. All I can give you is runway 14, two thousand four hundred metres. Can you work with that?
Listen to the controller's response and state your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, understood. Lakeside is forty miles north with a three thousand two hundred metre runway, weather is good there. Or I can ask how long until 09 is clear. Which do you want?

pre.text: Situation Update The tower advises that runway 09 will be clear in about ten minutes. You have finished the checklist and the landing gear will have to be extended by the alternate system.

body.text: Contact approach, give them an update of your situation and state what you will need for the landing.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, turn left heading 090, descend and maintain 3,000 until established, cleared for the ILS runway 09 approach, the equipment will be standing by, and let me know if anything changes.
Listen to the controller's question and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, my tower is asking whether you will be able to vacate the runway yourself, or whether they should plan on towing you off.

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
